units.text: Begin with the shared gateway on the left. VPN CloudHub connects multiple remote sites through a common virtual private gateway. Each site uses its own Site-to-Site VPN connection.

Move to the BGP panel. Give each customer gateway a unique autonomous system number and advertise nonoverlapping site prefixes. These identities and routes let the hub distinguish the connected sites.
Follow the route arrows in the third panel. The virtual private gateway re-advertises site routes to other sites. Verify that each customer device accepts the routes and permits the intended traffic.

With the full slide visible, separate this remote-site hub from VPC peering. CloudHub does not make peering transitive. Compare Transit Gateway when the network needs broader routing and segmentation.
Start with the identity panel. Client VPN supports certificate-based mutual authentication, Active Directory and federated SAML. Select a supported method that fits the organization's identity model.

Move to authorization on the upper right. Successful authentication establishes identity; authorization rules determine destination access. A connected client still needs permission and a working network path.

Inspect the lower-left network controls. Configure target connectivity, endpoint routes and destination security. Trace the return path as well as the outgoing request when diagnosing access failures.

Return to the full slide and the operations checklist. Plan client addressing, DNS, connection logs and highly available connectivity. Test access through every intended target path rather than only one successful connection.

Follow the split-tunnel diagram on the upper left. Endpoint routes are installed on the client, and matching destinations use the VPN. Other traffic follows the client's remaining routing configuration.

Move to the full-tunnel path. Client traffic travels through the VPN, so internet access needs a deliberate egress design. Verify routing and authorization instead of assuming that a connected tunnel provides internet access.
Inspect the lower-left destinations. Peered VPCs and on-premises networks require complete routes, authorization and return connectivity. Validate the full path separately for each destination.

With the full slide restored, examine Transit Gateway integration. Check its endpoint requirements and limitations: one endpoint cannot mix subnet and Transit Gateway associations, and network-based authorization is required for the Transit Gateway design.
Begin with the site-to-site diagram. SiteLink connects supported on-premises sites through Direct Connect locations. Its purpose is transport between sites using the AWS network.

Move to the virtual interfaces. Enable SiteLink on supported private or transit interfaces associated with the same Direct Connect gateway. Confirm the interface and gateway configuration at both ends.
Follow the direct path in the third panel. Site-to-site traffic can avoid traversing an AWS Region. Compare routing policy and wide-area-network needs before choosing the transport.

Return to the full slide and the warning panel. SiteLink does not eliminate access-circuit failures or automatically encrypt an application end to end. Design resilient access and the required encryption separately.
